findings.where: First screen, the line under the name: 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS', with the circled 'A' section marker to the left of 'MARK M. MOSELEY'. 'NTS' is repeated above the drawing and in the title block
findings.fault: The drawing-sheet captions sit in the identity line and get the same weight as the role. 'Infrastructure advisor' shares one block of tracked capitals with 'Longitudinal section A-A • Scale NTS', and a circled 'A' sits beside the name like a badge or an initial. In the five seconds a visitor gives the page, the line that should say who Mark is and what he does reads half as drafting notes. 'NTS' appears three times on the first screen.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff on a first visit, who want to see at once who Mark is and what he does. To them 'Longitudinal section A-A' is noise next to his name. Mark would object too, because the conceit speaks louder than his role.

findings.where: The whole tile: the first screen and every style-tile section
findings.fault: Mark is never shown. There is no photograph and no labelled placeholder for one anywhere: the first screen is the drawing, the name and the line. The brief asks every direction to answer client value 3 ('Mark is seen and heard'). First-visit trust item 1 asks a solo advisor's site to show a real face. This tile never shows how a portrait would sit on the diazo-blue gridded sheet, so the layout round inherits a look that has not shown it can carry Mark's photograph.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, choosing among the directions, cannot judge whether this one keeps 'the man himself'. A first-time visitor from a development bank gets no face to trust.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the hero drawing above 'MARK M. MOSELEY'
findings.fault: On phone the drawing shrinks to a thin strip about 120 px tall, wedged between the two-row title block and the name. The name, the paragraph and the amber button take most of the screen. The direction's one carried principle, the picture leading and the words waiting (client value 2, calm first), holds on desktop but is lost on phone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for one calm picture before any text asks for anything. Many visitors arriving from a LinkedIn link on a phone would see a text page with a small diagram, not the picture-first sheet.

findings.where: First screen: the loose S-curve at the right end of the hero drawing, rising from the ground line past the last pier to the frame edge
findings.fault: One thin curve leaves the section at the right, with no label and no counterpart on the left, and ends in mid-air. Every other line in the drawing is dimensioned or explained, so this one reads as a stray line or a leftover from the easing plot rather than part of the aqueduct.
findings.who_objects: Mark, an engineer-adjacent reader whose 'blueprint paper' idea depends on the drawing looking exact. An unexplained line makes it look unfinished.

findings.where: Article specimen (desktop and phone): the post body and pull quote set over the full blueprint grid
findings.fault: The article page keeps the homepage sheet's full grid of minor and major lines behind the running prose, so grid lines cross every line of text. On the homepage the grid is atmosphere. On a long article, read in Read mode, it makes the page look busy under the words, and it travels to every post Angélique adds.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading one of Mark's longer articles, for whom ruled lines crossing every line of text become tiring. Mark, who finds busy sites off-putting.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel: the timing note '(#13, F5/F12)' and the easing column's 'plot'
findings.fault: Internal ticket and research references and an unexplained shorthand ('plot') are printed on the tile itself. The panel reads as a working file, not a direction shown to the client.
findings.who_objects: Mark, the tile's reader, who has no access to tickets #13 or F5/F12 and cannot tell what 'plot' means as an easing.
